title: Prefix writer and tee logger
hints: A line can be split across `Write` calls, so the writer needs **memory** between calls: a field like `midLine bool` that says whether the next byte continues a line or starts a new one. That's why `Write` has a pointer receiver.

Build the output in a fresh `[]byte` (never modify `p`): loop over the bytes; if `!midLine`, append the prefix and set `midLine = true`; append the byte; if it was `'\n'`, set `midLine = false`. Then make one `Write` to the wrapped writer.

Store the prefix as `[]byte` so you can `out = append(out, pw.prefix...)`. After the wrapped write: `if err != nil { return 0, err }`, save the new `midLine` state, `return len(p), nil`. `NewLogger` is one line: `return NewPrefixWriter(io.MultiWriter(ws...), prefix)`.
